name: Spritz Sans
classification_notes: Low-contrast display sans with sharp, expressive letterforms rooted in Art Nouveau lettering traditions. Part of a variable type system where the Sans and Serif subfamilies share a common structural skeleton, with a Serif variable axis bridging the two voices.
summary: Art Nouveau-inspired variable sans with sharp expressive letterforms sharing a skeleton with its Serif sibling.
description: Spritz Sans is the low-contrast half of a variable type system that shares a structural skeleton with Spritz Serif, bridged by a Serif variable axis. The letterforms are sharp and expressive, drawing on Art Nouveau ornamental traditions while keeping contrast minimal. Best suited to display settings, editorial work and branding in Latin or Cyrillic.
foundry_blurb: About Type describes Spritz as an eclectic Sans and Serif variable type system inspired by the ornamental richness of Art Nouveau lettering. The Sans and Serif share a common structure but offer contrasting voices: the Sans delivers minimal contrast and sharp, expressive letterforms, while the Serif adds higher contrast, pronounced serifs and angled terminals. The system includes six stylistic sets covering alternate letterforms and locale-specific Cyrillic variants for Bulgarian and Serbian.
